texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Watts Chapel in Surrey is an Arts and Crafts masterpiece with vivid colors, decorations, and symbols on wood, terracotta, and plaster of Paris.
texts.text: The Watts Chapel in Surrey is an Arts and Crafts masterpiece with vivid colors, decorations, and symbols on wood, terracotta, and plaster of Paris.

texts.orig: Watts Chapel exterior of brick and terracotta.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The construction of Watts Chapel began in 1896 when the Celtic Revival movement was part of Arts and Crafts work created at the time. Located in the village of Compton near Guildford, the chapel is now considered a late 19th century Arts and Crafts masterpiece.
texts.text: The construction of Watts Chapel began in 1896 when the Celtic Revival movement was part of Arts and Crafts work created at the time. Located in the village of Compton near Guildford, the chapel is now considered a late 19th century Arts and Crafts masterpiece.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Mary Seton Watts (1849-1938) was a Scottish artist who worked with clay, metal, and textiles in the Celtic and British Art Nouveau styles. She also worked to create employment for rural communities through the preservation of handicrafts, including a pottery guild in the village of Compton in Surrey.
texts.text: Mary Seton Watts (1849-1938) was a Scottish artist who worked with clay, metal, and textiles in the Celtic and British Art Nouveau styles. She also worked to create employment for rural communities through the preservation of handicrafts, including a pottery guild in the village of Compton in Surrey.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Watts Chapel became an example of public participation art with more than 70 villagers involved in the chapel's construction and decoration between 1896 and 1904.
texts.text: The Watts Chapel became an example of public participation art with more than 70 villagers involved in the chapel's construction and decoration between 1896 and 1904.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: While Mary Watts was the artistic force behind the chapel project, George Tunstal Redmayne (1840-1912) was the architect.
texts.text: While Mary Watts was the artistic force behind the chapel project, George Tunstal Redmayne (1840-1912) was the architect.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The April 1966 issue of (a British magazine) described the chapel as a curious edifice with a richness of color. Perhaps too rich. The Connoisseur
texts.text: The April 1966 issue of (a British magazine) described the chapel as a curious edifice with a richness of color. Perhaps too rich. The Connoisseur

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 'It looms excessively red on its green hillside, strident like a London bus has strayed down a country lane...the result of the use of a local clay for the bricks. '
texts.text: 'It looms excessively red on its green hillside, strident like a London bus has strayed down a country lane...the result of the use of a local clay for the bricks. '

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Mary Watts was aware of the effect of the red bricks and hoped the red color would tone down.
texts.text: Mary Watts was aware of the effect of the red bricks and hoped the red color would tone down.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 'it is growing every day less red, and the green enfolds it all so beautifully now, the trees are in leaf...a sweet resting place. '
texts.text: 'it is growing every day less red, and the green enfolds it all so beautifully now, the trees are in leaf...a sweet resting place. '

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Today's visitors can see that the red bricks of the Watts Chapel have, in fact, toned down.
texts.text: Today's visitors can see that the red bricks of the Watts Chapel have, in fact, toned down.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Modeled on the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem, the chapel stands on the side of Budburrow Hill and faces east toward Jerusalem.
texts.text: Modeled on the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem, the chapel stands on the side of Budburrow Hill and faces east toward Jerusalem.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The outside of the chapel is covered with decorative clay tiles, molded by members of the local community.
texts.text: The outside of the chapel is covered with decorative clay tiles, molded by members of the local community.

texts.label: caption
texts.orig: Watts Chapel exterior with decorative clay tiles.
texts.text: Watts Chapel exterior with decorative clay tiles.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 'The flower that closes with the setting sun and opens again when darkness is past. '
texts.text: 'The flower that closes with the setting sun and opens again when darkness is past. '

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Crafted to Mary Watts' design, the terracotta tiles blend Celtic, Romanesque, and Art Nouveau influences.
texts.text: Crafted to Mary Watts' design, the terracotta tiles blend Celtic, Romanesque, and Art Nouveau influences.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The chapel's   Celtic Romanesque entrance has a semicircular arch supported by three pillars. The design is taken from early Irish churches, such as Clonfert Cathedral in County Galway, Ireland.
texts.text: The chapel's   Celtic Romanesque entrance has a semicircular arch supported by three pillars. The design is taken from early Irish churches, such as Clonfert Cathedral in County Galway, Ireland.

texts.label: caption
texts.orig: The chapel door carved from chestnut and oak.
texts.text: The chapel door carved from chestnut and oak.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The three-tiered arch above the door features a Celtic knot of interlaced hearts at the top, followed by a row of peacock feathers, and then a row of 15 angels. The faces of the angels look up in hope or down in sympathy.
texts.text: The three-tiered arch above the door features a Celtic knot of interlaced hearts at the top, followed by a row of peacock feathers, and then a row of 15 angels. The faces of the angels look up in hope or down in sympathy.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The chapel door was carved from chestnut and oak by the Compton wheelwright Thomas Steadman. The door's wrought iron was forged by the village blacksmith Clarence Sex.
texts.text: The chapel door was carved from chestnut and oak by the Compton wheelwright Thomas Steadman. The door's wrought iron was forged by the village blacksmith Clarence Sex.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The symbols on the doors include crosses, flames, wings, and the slaying of a dragon. Visually, the wrought iron cross acts as a mast for sails on either side of the door panels.
texts.text: The symbols on the doors include crosses, flames, wings, and the slaying of a dragon. Visually, the wrought iron cross acts as a mast for sails on either side of the door panels.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: With four naves of equal length and width,   the chapel is in the shape of a Byzantine Greek cross.
texts.text: With four naves of equal length and width,   the chapel is in the shape of a Byzantine Greek cross.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The chapel's round shape - a never-ending circle - symbolizes the promise of an everlasting life with the cupola at the top representing the dome of heaven rising from the earth.
texts.text: The chapel's round shape - a never-ending circle - symbolizes the promise of an everlasting life with the cupola at the top representing the dome of heaven rising from the earth.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The interior decorations are made from felt, string, and chicken wire, dipped in plaster, and painted over the surface.
texts.text: The interior decorations are made from felt, string, and chicken wire, dipped in plaster, and painted over the surface.

texts.label: caption
texts.orig: Painted decorations in Art Nouveau style.
texts.text: Painted decorations in Art Nouveau style.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Inside the chapel, you will find an unusual altar painting by Mary's husband, George Frederic Watts.
texts.text: Inside the chapel, you will find an unusual altar painting by Mary's husband, George Frederic Watts.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: George Frederic Watts (1817-1904) was a sought-after portrait artist in the Victorian age, with portrait commissions from the English poet, Robert Browning to the British monarch, King Edward VII. These commissioned portraits financed the construction of Watts Chapel.
texts.text: George Frederic Watts (1817-1904) was a sought-after portrait artist in the Victorian age, with portrait commissions from the English poet, Robert Browning to the British monarch, King Edward VII. These commissioned portraits financed the construction of Watts Chapel.

texts.label: caption
texts.orig: The All-Pervading in the Watts Gallery.
texts.text: The All-Pervading in the Watts Gallery.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: An allegorical painting produced between 1887 and 1890, was influenced by the Sibyls of the Sistine Chapel ceiling and symbolizes the spirit that George Frederic Watts saw as governing 'the immeasurable expanse'. The All-Pervading
texts.text: An allegorical painting produced between 1887 and 1890, was influenced by the Sibyls of the Sistine Chapel ceiling and symbolizes the spirit that George Frederic Watts saw as governing 'the immeasurable expanse'. The All-Pervading

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In 1899, Watts presented the painting to the Tate in London. is now on loan from Tate Britain to the Watts Gallery. The All-Pervading
texts.text: In 1899, Watts presented the painting to the Tate in London. is now on loan from Tate Britain to the Watts Gallery. The All-Pervading

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A smaller version of the painting is the altarpiece for the Watts Chapel.
texts.text: A smaller version of the painting is the altarpiece for the Watts Chapel.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: George Frederic Watts died in 1904, just three months after completing the altar painting.
texts.text: George Frederic Watts died in 1904, just three months after completing the altar painting.

texts.text: Tips for the Watts Chapel in Surrey

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Wear appropriate footwear. The path is steep, curved, and partly cobblestoned.
texts.text: Wear appropriate footwear. The path is steep, curved, and partly cobblestoned.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Occasionally, the chapel is closed for private services. Please check opening times before visiting.
texts.text: Occasionally, the chapel is closed for private services. Please check opening times before visiting.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Arrive early (on a weekday, if possible). Keep in mind that the Friday tours are from 12:301:30pm (if volunteer guides are available).
texts.text: Arrive early (on a weekday, if possible). Keep in mind that the Friday tours are from 12:301:30pm (if volunteer guides are available).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Go immediately to the chapel. While the chapel's regular hours may be 10am-5pm, we found the door was unlocked at 9:45am, which meant we had the chapel interior and exterior to ourselves until 10:35am, when the next visitors arrived.
texts.text: Go immediately to the chapel. While the chapel's regular hours may be 10am-5pm, we found the door was unlocked at 9:45am, which meant we had the chapel interior and exterior to ourselves until 10:35am, when the next visitors arrived.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Walk farther up the hill. There, you will see the final resting places of Mary and George Watts, and a view of the chapel's bell turret.
texts.text: Walk farther up the hill. There, you will see the final resting places of Mary and George Watts, and a view of the chapel's bell turret.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: See the wellhead. Near the entrance to the cemetery stands a wellhead built in 1906. While the well is no longer in use, the wellhead is decorated with terracotta panels.
